inputs.basis: Horizon revenue per earning IT MW and the actual modeled contract/spot revenue mix feed the shared steady-state DCF. Company running-cost margins and maintenance assumptions are retained. A 55% refresh reserve every four years plus 3% annual spares is a long-run house allowance, not compulsory retirement at a contract expiry. Post-horizon market growth of 6% for five years is a separate house assumption; new/renewed contracts reprice every three years in that terminal regime.

steady.footer: $3.80m normalized cash per earning IT MW; 3.42× revenue from the shared DCF.
steady.basis: Horizon revenue per earning IT MW and the actual modeled contract/spot revenue mix feed the shared steady-state DCF. Company running-cost margins and maintenance assumptions are retained. A 55% refresh reserve every four years plus 3% annual spares is a long-run house allowance, not compulsory retirement at a contract expiry. Post-horizon market growth of 6% for five years is a separate house assumption; new/renewed contracts reprice every three years in that terminal regime.

prepay.basis: weighted-average prepayment 15-25% of TCV at signing (424B4/10-K), credited against billings in the final months of the contract; at the 20% midpoint on a 5-yr contract at $14m per MW-yr that is $14m per MW, ~42% of the $33m GPU cost; deferred revenue $9.7bn at 30-Jun-26 (10-Q) is the opening balance, credited half in-window (2028-30) and half after 2030 (OpenAI to May-31, Meta to Dec-32) Modeled future receipts retain the capex-based funding assumption; they are not secured financing. Inferred credits use modeled service start and contract expiry: final four quarters. Explicit opening-balance credits and special receipts retain their own dated schedules. Mixed future tranches allocate inferred credits by contractual IT MW; purchase capex remains scheduled if delivery slips.

finance.wfMarginBasis: the quarterly waterfall runs at the printed 57% adjusted EBITDA margin (Q4-25 to Q2-26: 57/56/59%); the per-MW multiple uses 60%, a mature-MW margin between the print and management’s ~70% contract-level zone
finance.basis: debt 8% (senior notes 9.0-9.75%, DDTL 4.0 SOFR+225/5.9% fixed, DDTL 5.0/5.5 SOFR+450/550, OEM financing; converts 1.75%), 16%/yr pool amortisation (DDTLs amortise over 5 yrs, notes bullet), $3bn cash floor; lenders advance 90% of GPU cost on contracted capacity (DDTL 4.0 90% LTC), 50% on spot; the shell is leased (rent inside EBITDA, no shell capex, lease liabilities not double-counted as debt); 10% of capex from 2027 as policy equity at $90 plus the residual; converts (2031 $2.59bn at $107.80 cap $215.60; 2032 $4.0bn at $119.60 cap $230) convert at the model 2030 price; restricted cash $1.4bn counted; fully diluted count before converts 608.5m = 551.5m basic (31 Jul 26) + 24m options at $1.84 + 4m warrants at $1.55 + 29m RSUs

power: MW active at 30 June · 4.2 GW contracted

notes: 4.2 GW contracted, 1.5 GW active. Fifty-one leased data centres; no single provider delivers more than 17% of active power. Every site is rented — Core Scientific (590 MW), Applied Digital (400 MW), Galaxy Helios (525 MW), Chirisa, TierPoint, Flexential.Q2-26 10-Q · 11 Aug call

The bottleneck is powered shell, not GPUs or grid. One lessor running late cost the 2025 active-power target 50 MW and cut FY25 capex from $20–23bn to $12–14bn; the delayed sites landed in Q1-26.Q3-25 and Q4-25 calls
2030: “at least 8 GW”. Contracted 4.2 GW plus >1.5 GW of powered land, options and LOIs is ~6 GW; the model carries 7 GW by end-2030 and leaves the rest unmodelled.Q2-26 call · tracker pipeline
~850k GPUs by Dec 2026 on 1.85 GW active. The company reported >250k GPUs at end-2024 on 360 MW; density per MW falls as Blackwell and Rubin racks replace Hopper.10-K FY25 · model densities

Six-year book life. Technology equipment is depreciated over six years (five before 2023); management points to A100s re-contracted into 2029 and H100 pricing within 10% of a year earlier.10-K Note 2 · Q4-25 and Q2-26 calls

Vera Rubin from Q4-27. Meta’s $21bn order and Jane Street’s $6bn commitment are the first Vera Rubin deployments; CoreWeave took delivery of the first VR NVL72 rack in June 2026.8-K 9 Apr 2026 · 8-K 15 Apr 2026

Contract cohorts. Existing/inferred book keeps its original all-in rate until a disclosed or estimated expiry. Expiry ends signed coverage; continuation becomes an assumed renewal. New capacity uses one shared house curve.

Compare matching measures. Annualized earning contracted revenue divided by earning contracted IT MW measures contract yield. Total annualized revenue divided by all earning IT MW includes spot. Neither denominator should be paired with full energized-capacity ARR.

Evidence. Every tranche records price, commitment and expiry provenance. An inferred allocation is not a verified contract. New prices, zero software premium and 100% same-hardware renewal continuation are explicit assumptions.

Success-based capex. Contracted revenue more than covers capex within the contract term; each deployment is financed by a self-amortising delayed-draw term loan plus prepayments. DDTL 4.0 ($8.5bn, SOFR+225 / 5.9% fixed, non-recourse, A3) advances 90% of cost; DDTL 5.5 ($2.6bn, SOFR+550) finances 3-year contracts.8-Ks 30 Mar, 15 May, 7 Aug 2026

“Weighted-average cost of debt down almost 300 bps in a year.” $35.6bn of debt at 30 June: DDTLs $13.6bn, senior notes $10.0bn at 9–9.75%, converts $6.6bn at 1.75%, OEM financing $4.8bn. Interest ran $640m in Q2 against $1.51bn of adjusted EBITDA.Q2-26 10-Q Note 8 · 11 Aug call

The catch: prepayments are 15–25% of contract value and lenders advance 90% only against signed take-or-pay. Unsigned capacity needs ~$16.5m of equity per MW — or, as in 2025, the NVIDIA backstop and equity placements ($2bn at $87.20, $1bn at $109).424B4 · 8-Ks 23 Jan, 15 Apr 2026

Common calculation, different costs. The steady-state multiple is recomputed from horizon earned revenue per IT MW. Company margins, leased or owned shell costs, maintenance, tax and discount assumptions remain explicit.

Equipment life is separate. A contract expiry does not remove the GPUs or install a newer generation. Existing equipment renews at its own rate; the long-run maintenance reserve is a house assumption.
Reconciled value. Updated quarterly revenue passes through the existing debt, prepayment and dilution waterfall. The terminal multiple is recalculated from the displayed steady-state inputs.
Separate clocks. Model policy revision is dated 15 September 2026; financial disclosures and reference share prices retain their original dates. This is not a refreshed market quotation.

arr.cap: Annualized earned revenue is split into existing book (including estimates), assumed renewals, assumed new contracts and spot. Full-capacity contracted run-rate is a separate measure.

footer.sources: Q2-26 10-Q (filed 12 Aug 2026), Q1-26 10-Q, FY25 10-K (2 Mar 2026), IPO 424B4; 8-Ks for DDTL 3.0/4.0/5.0/5.5, both convertible issues, the senior notes, the NVIDIA and Jane Street placements, the OpenAI, Meta and NVIDIA order forms; FactSet corrected transcripts Q1-25 to Q2-26 (IR CDN); Core Scientific, Applied Digital and Galaxy filings for lease terms; Epoch AI satellite site assessments; SemiAnalysis ClusterMAX and public GPU index.
footer.model: Shared pricing and contract-cohort model. Existing commitments, estimated coverage, same-hardware renewals and new business are distinguished. Pricing, expiry and continuity assumptions are exposed with their evidence. Company financing and capex retain the dated research snapshot.

capexBasis: GPUs + ancillaries per active MW by vintage: $30m Blackwell (derived $25-37m from management capex ÷ active MW added, FY25 and H1-26), +10% on 2027 orders, Rubin ~$38m, next-gen ~$45m; no shell capex — every data centre is leased (10-K: “we lease all of our existing data centers”; $35.5bn of signed-not-commenced leases at 30-Jun-26)

market.units: USD millions per IT MW per year; all-in contracted services
market.tenorBasis: The initial new-business curve has no calibrated tenor premium or discount. Term controls the next renewal date. A five-year, 15% lower-price case is an explicit sensitivity, not a disclosed market spread.
market.generationBasis: The shared frontier curve is quoted per IT MW, with generation factors of 1 as an explicit house assumption. It is not a hardware productivity forecast. Existing equipment renews at its own all-in price; renewal does not install new GPUs.

renewal.basis: Base assumes the same hardware keeps earning at the original all-in rate and 100% contracted capacity renews. These are house assumptions, not commitments. Price and retention downside cases are shown.

spot.note: Shared realized spot assumptions inherited from the CoreWeave/Nebius model, not executable rate cards. Physical GPU density remains tranche-specific.

market.basis: One shared new-business curve using the existing Nebius 2027–30 house ladder ($18m/$19m/$20m/$21m per IT MW-year). Prices fix at modeled service commencement, not energisation. Current disclosures support improving pricing but do not establish these forward prices. Existing/inferred commitments retain their own rates through disclosed or estimated expiry. No quantified company software premium is assumed. The 2031 service-start price holds the 2030 level flat; it is a house extension, not a market quote.

limitations: Expiry quarters are estimates from modeled acceptance unless specifically marked disclosed.
An inferred existing-book allocation is not a verified customer commitment for that physical tranche.
Renewals do not retire or replace equipment. The long-run maintenance reserve is a separate house assumption.
Contract price by tenor is uncalibrated in the base case; the five-year discount is an explicit sensitivity.
Future prepayments and borrowing capacity are financing assumptions, not committed funding; customer credits follow modeled contract terms.
Delivery-delay tests retain the original capex purchase calendar. Fixed opening credit schedules remain unchanged.
Any prepayment balance without a credit calendar is deducted at face value at the horizon until its timing is sourced.
Forecast cash margin is 57%; normalized terminal margin is 60%.

Unmapped future tranches energizing from 2027Q1 use the shared new-business curve. Power leases do not establish customer compute prices. Existing and in-flight 2026 book and identifiable disclosed future commitments retain their own rates. This cutoff is a house allocation convention, not a statement that disclosed backlog excludes future sites. The legacy-book-allocation sensitivity tests the uncertainty.

sensitivities.label: Joint downside
